synonyms: Sapindus saponaria var. drummondii (Hook. & Arn.) L.D.Benson
Sapindus saponaria subsp. drummondii (Hook. & Arn.) A.E.Murray
taxonomic_note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Sapindus drummondii Hook. & Arn. and treats Sapindus saponaria var. drummondii as a homotypic synonym. Older Texas references still commonly use the varietal name; those source rows are one learner concept, not separate species.
look_here_first: Start with the fruiting branch. Western soapberry has alternate pinnately compound leaves with strongly asymmetric leaflets and clusters of round translucent amber-yellow drupes that often persist into winter. Then confirm the small cream flowers and floral disk.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Current 25-county target-zone support: Hays — UT PRC Hays flora lists western soapberry as Sapindus saponaria var. drummondii; Travis — UT PRC Travis County Sapindaceae index lists the same concept; Kerr — herbarium specimen from near Ingram under Sapindus drummondii; Williamson — UT PRC Williamson County flora documents S. saponaria var. drummondii; Val Verde — Powell's Trees and Shrubs of the Trans-Pecos explicitly lists Val Verde for S. saponaria var. drummondii. Current Kew/POWO accepts the historical var./subsp. drummondii concept as Sapindus drummondii.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Project threshold is >=3 counties from workflow/target-zone-counties.json. Williamson and Val Verde are valid target-zone counties under the current 2026-09-30 definition. B160's earlier outside-zone statement was corrected the same day. Historical var./subsp. drummondii records map to current Sapindus drummondii, not Sapindus saponaria sensu stricto.

best_field_traits: deciduous small tree, often clonal and thicket-forming
leaves alternate, once-pinnately compound, without stipules
leaflets usually numerous and conspicuously asymmetric at the base
small cream to whitish flowers in branched terminal clusters
floral disk present around the superior ovary
round fleshy one-seeded drupes ripening yellow to amber and becoming translucent
fruit clusters often persist after leaf fall
morphology_keys.leaves: Alternate pinnate leaves usually carry many asymmetrical lanceolate leaflets; the missing terminal leaflet and unequal leaflet bases are useful field cues.
morphology_keys.flower: Small pale flowers occur in branched clusters. A floral disk is part of the Sapindaceae reproductive plan.
morphology_keys.fruit: Round one-seeded drupes become yellow to amber and translucent; the saponin-rich pericarp gives the tree its soapberry name.
morphology_keys.field_tip: Without fruit, compare the alternate pinnate leaves carefully against Rhus and Pistacia. With fruit, the translucent soapberry drupes are highly distinctive.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Ungnadia has a thick 3-lobed woody capsule with large glossy seeds; Sapindus has round translucent one-seeded drupes. Boxelder has opposite compound leaves and paired samaras. Sumacs generally show different fruit clusters and lack the translucent soapberry fruit.
